UnitStatement: DEL-10-04 is a TEST_SUITE deliverable under PKG-10 (Domain Engine Future Boundary) for domain profile validation and an OpenPipeStress fixture.
DEL-10-04 belongs to DecompositionVariant SOFTWARE_DECOMP at DecompositionRevision v3.2.
DEL-10-04 is future-boundary/gated scope, not current-release domain operation execution.
No human owner is assigned for interpreting future fixture pass/fail validation evidence (TBD).
The DomainEngineProfile contract fields are profileId, engineName, optional engineVersion, protectedPaths, proposalPaths, artifactTypes, operations, manifestRules, and boundaryNotice.

OperationProposal validation-relevant fields are proposal identity, profile identity, operation name, inputs, intended changes, deterministic checks, expected outputs, risks, required human gate, and status.
OpenPipeStress is a potential first domain profile fixture, not Chirality core runtime behavior.
Domain profile validation is deterministic; invalid or incomplete profiles fail before runtime exposure (FR-109).
Protected domain-engine paths are not directly agent-writable (FR-110; K-DOMAIN-2).
Domain-engine output is not professional approval, code compliance, external validation, or Chirality-owned solver truth (FR-115; K-DOMAIN-4).
Domain-engine profiles and operation proposals are future amendment work after core harness stability (PLAN R7).
Domain-engine endpoints and tools are provisional future interfaces and must not be implemented as current-release scope (SPEC Section 18).
Prompt text is not a sufficient safety boundary for filesystem writes or domain operations (K-PERM-2).
OpenPipeStress-specific assumptions must live in profile and adapter layers, not in core harness runtime (FR-114).
An accepted PKG-10 amendment or explicit human authorization is required before fixture implementation becomes active work.
No accepted OpenPipeStress fixture file exists in this deliverable yet (TBD).
Validation tests should provide deterministic checks for required profile fields, path separation, manifest rules, operation descriptors, and boundary notices.
An adapter assumptions note should separate OpenPipeStress profile/adapter assumptions from Chirality core runtime behavior.
DEL-10-04 keeps future Domain Engine Profile validation and an OpenPipeStress fixture representable without turning Chirality into a domain-specific solver.
FR-107 requires a generic DomainEngineProfile contract before engine-specific integration.
K-DOMAIN-2 and FR-110/FR-111 require agents to write proposals and summaries, not protected domain-engine model truth.
K-DOMAIN-3 and FR-113 require explicit human acceptance before applying domain operations.
K-AUTH-1 and K-DOMAIN-4 prohibit representing agent, runtime, or domain adapter output as professional approval, code compliance, external validation, or Chirality-owned solver truth.
The future fixture should test the generic shape first: identity, protected paths, proposal paths, artifact types, operations, manifest rules, and boundary notices.
OpenPipeStress can be a concrete profile fixture only after the generic profile boundary is accepted by amendment; until then its specific values and semantics remain TBD.

A useful future validation suite should include negative cases such as missing boundary notice, protected path listed as proposal path, missing deterministic adapter manifest rule, incomplete operation descriptor, or wording implying Chirality owns solver truth.

Future adapter assumptions should separate four classes: profile-level fixture facts, adapter-level manifest/execution assumptions, operation-proposal human-gated change assumptions, and explicit core-runtime non-assumptions.
The REF-006 PRD hash mismatch is a visible source-status warning, not a new design fact; closure reliance still needs human acceptance or refreshed source metadata.

A future positive fixture should be a generic DomainEngineProfile instance for openpipestress with required fields, protected/proposal path separation, operation descriptors, manifest rules, and boundary notice.
Negative case: missing boundaryNotice.
Negative case: protectedPaths and proposalPaths overlap.
Negative case: operation descriptor lacks deterministic checks.
Negative case: fixture text states or implies Chirality approves engineering work.
Negative case: OpenPipeStress behavior is asserted as core harness runtime behavior.
CT-001: no source-content conflict identified during P1/P2; the PRD hash mismatch is recorded as a source warning only, with human ruling TBD.
The procedure defines producing and later verifying the DEL-10-04 future fixture profile, validation tests, and adapter assumptions note without activating domain-engine implementation.
Prerequisite: an accepted PKG-10 amendment or explicit human authorization for future domain-engine work.
Step: verify PKG-10 remains future-boundary/gated scope unless a human-approved amendment says otherwise.
Step: do not create or activate domain-engine endpoints, protected-path write behavior, or operation-apply workflows during this deliverable-local drafting run.
Step: use docs/TYPES.md Section 11.1 as the candidate DomainEngineProfile shape.
Step: mark any field semantics not defined by the accessible source corpus as TBD.
Step: keep OpenPipeStress solver assumptions in the profile or adapter-assumptions layer.
Step: do not add OpenPipeStress assumptions to Chirality core runtime.
Validation check: required profile fields are present.
Validation check: protected/proposal path separation.
Validation check: operation descriptors against OperationProposal concepts where operation fixtures are present.
Validation check: deterministic adapter manifest presence, or mark manifest rules TBD.
Validation check: boundary notice presence.
For each negative case, record the deterministic expected failure or mark the expected output TBD.
Negative validation case: operation fixture without required human gate.
Step: in the adapter assumptions note, separate accepted source facts from ASSUMPTION and TBD items.
Step: confirm no current-release endpoint/tool activation was introduced.
Step: confirm ResponsibleParty remains TBD.
The specification is limited to future-boundary test-suite definition and source-grounded fixture expectations for PKG-10.

The deliverable excludes current-release activation of domain-engine endpoints, domain-operation application, protected-model writes, solver integration, and any claim that Chirality approves or owns domain-engine solver truth.

Before becoming executable work, a human-approved PKG-10 amendment must identify the ResponsibleParty, concrete test path, adapter manifest location, evidence-record format, and expected-failure fixtures.
DEL-10-04-REQ-001: the validation posture shall treat DomainEngineProfile as a future platform contract, not current core runtime behavior.

DEL-10-04-REQ-002: a profile validation fixture shall cover the generic profile fields including profileId, engineName, optional engineVersion, protectedPaths, proposalPaths, artifactTypes, operations, manifestRules, and boundaryNotice.
DEL-10-04-REQ-003: validation shall be deterministic and shall fail invalid or incomplete profiles before runtime exposure.
DEL-10-04-REQ-004: the OpenPipeStress fixture shall be represented as a fixture profile only, with its assumptions held in profile and adapter layers rather than Chirality core runtime.
DEL-10-04-REQ-005: profile validation shall preserve separation between protected paths and proposal paths.

DEL-10-04-REQ-006: operation-related fixture data shall align with OperationProposal concepts before application: inputs, intended changes, deterministic checks, expected outputs, risks, and required human gate.
DEL-10-04-REQ-007: boundary notices shall state that Chirality does not provide professional approval, code compliance, external validation, or Chirality-owned solver truth.
DEL-10-04-REQ-008: the fixture/test suite shall not rely on prompt-only restrictions for protected paths or domain operations.
DEL-10-04-REQ-009: the deliverable shall preserve the PRD hash mismatch as a source warning rather than accepted truth drift.
DEL-10-04-REQ-010: future negative tests shall define deterministic expected failures, not only checklist labels.

DEL-10-04-REQ-011: future operation-descriptor fixtures shall cover inputs, intended changes, deterministic checks, expected outputs, risks, required human gate, and status before any operation can be applied.
DEL-10-04-REQ-012: future fixture validation shall produce stable evidence records for pass/fail determinations and boundary-notice wording coverage.
REF-006: docs/PRD.md expected SHA256 86cb6fb9...eb34 differs from observed SHA256 fb1c73f7...6fc8, treated as a source warning only per assignment override.
